nodes.name: Hydrothermal Mn-Ni LDH growth
nodes.procedure: Mn-doped Ni LDH-coated NF (Mn-Ni LDH/NF) was prepared by immersing a cleaned NF into a solution containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (3 mmol), Mn(NO3)2·4H2O (0.15 mmol), NH4F (7 mmol), and urea (15 mmol) in 80 mL deionized water, followed by hydrothermal treatment at 120°C for 6 h. The product was washed and dried.
nodes.source_text: Mn-doped Ni LDH-coated NF (Mn-Ni LDH/NF) was prepared by immersing a cleaned NF into a solution containing Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (3 mmol), Mn(NO3)2·4H2O (0.15 mmol), NH4F (7 mmol), and urea (15 mmol) in 80 mL deionized water, followed by hydrothermal treatment at 120°C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Phytic acid modification
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, Mn-Ni LDH was immersed in a solution of phytic acid (1.5 mL in 25 mL deionized water) for 30 min and then reacted at 70°C for 6 h to form Mn-Ni-PA. After washing and drying.

nodes.name: Iridium single atom immobilization
nodes.procedure: After washing and drying, Mn-Ni-PA was soaked in 0.05 mmol IrCl3 xH2O in 100 mL deionized water solution and reacted at 50°C for 8 h, yielding Ir@Mn-Ni-PA. The final product was thoroughly washed and dried for further characterization.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hierarchical nanosheet array structure remains largely intact after PA modification and Ir incorporation (Figure 2a,b).
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images at different magnifications (Figure 2a,b) reveal that the hierarchical nanosheet array structure of Mn-Ni LDH remains largely intact after PA surface modification and atomic-level Ir incorporation.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanosheets consist of interconnected nanoparticles with slight surface etching from PA treatment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanosheets consist of interconnected nanoparticles (Figure S2), with slight surface etching observed as a result of PA treatment.

properties.description: High-resolution image showing nanostructure with 2 nm scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM confirms numerous single Ir atoms on Mn-Ni-PA surface as bright atomic-scale spots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM (High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM) analysis further confirms the successful immobilization of numerous single Ir atoms on the Mn-Ni-PA surface, as indicated by the bright atomic-scale spots (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice fringes corresponding to (101) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ (2.33 Å) and (110) planes of Mn-doped α-Ni(OH)₂ (1.54 Å).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, in High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) inset Figure 2c, the observed lattice fringes correspond to the (101) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂ and the (110) planes of Mn-doped α-Ni(OH)₂, with interplanar spacings of 2.33 and 1.54 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms β-Ni(OH)₂ (001, 101 planes at 19.1°, 38.5°) and α-Ni(OH)₂ (003, 006 planes at 11.3°, 22.8°) phases with slight negative shift indicating Mn doping; no distinct Ir or Mn peaks suggesting atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 2d) further confirm that the composites retain identical structural phases, with no distinct peaks attributable to Ir or Mn, suggesting these elements are atomically dispersed.

properties.description: X-ray diffraction pattern showing peak at θ = 12.2°

nodes.characterization_summary: BET specific surface area of 36.8 m²/g indicates highly porous architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area measured by the Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) of Ir@Mn-Ni-PA is 36.8 m² g⁻¹, indicative of a highly porous architecture.

nodes.characterization_summary: Contact angle reduced to 12.2° after PA modification, enhancing hydrophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: PA modification enhanced hydrophilicity, reducing the contact angle to 12.2°.

properties.description: Image of a water droplet on the surface

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Mn, P, O, and Ir across catalyst surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping (Figure 2h) demonstrates a uniform distribution of Ni, Mn, P, O, and Ir across the catalyst surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir and Mn atomic percentages are 1.42% and 6.43%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) revealed Ir and Mn atomic percentages at 1.42% and 6.43%, respectively, in line with the designed composition (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mn 2p peaks at 653.3 and 646.7 eV; O 1s peaks at 530.4 (M-O), 531.6 (M-OH), 533.2 eV (H-OH); P 2p at 133.2 eV; Ir 4f peaks at 61.9 and 65.0 eV (Figure S3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Mn 2p + Ni Auger spectrum (Figure 3a) exhibits distinct peaks at 653.3 and 646.7 eV... The high-resolution P 2p spectrum (Figure 3c) exhibits a distinct peak at 133.2 eV... the deconvoluted Ir 4f + Ni 3p spectrum (Figure 3d) displays... peaks at 61.9 and 65.0 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L₃-edge XANES white line position aligns with IrO₂, indicating Ir oxidation state ~+4; higher white-line intensity suggests increased unoccupied Ir 5d states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra (Figure 3e) of Ir@Mn-Ni-PA, Ir powder, and IrO₂ reveal crucial insights into the oxidation state and electronic properties of Ir in the synthesized catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows dominant peak at ~1.7 Å indicating Ir-O bonds, absence of Ir-Ir coordination confirming atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis further elucidated the bonding environment around Ir atoms. As shown in Figure 3f, the dominant peak at ∼1.7 Å in Ir powder corresponds to Ir-Ir coordination, while IrO₂ exhibits a peak at the same position, attributed to Ir-O coordination. In contrast, the Ir@Mn-Ni-PA catalyst exclusively displays a peak at ∼1.7 Å, signifying the presence of Ir-O bonds and the absence of Ir-Ir coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region gives C_dl of 28.6 mF cm⁻², indicating large ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of Ir@Mn-Ni-PA reached 28.6 mF cm⁻², significantly higher than that of the control samples, reflecting a significantly larger electrochemically accessible surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistance of 1.51 Ω.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among all samples, Ir@Mn-Ni-PA catalyst exhibited the lowest charge transfer resistance of 1.51 Ω.
